svg.title: Sphere impostor geometry and shading
svg.desc: Ray-sphere geometry of a shaded impostor and the literal pixels of a 20 pixel sphere shaded by the implemented light.
svg.text: a sphere is a disc plus an analytic normal
Frame::ball and ball_fragment: no mesh, one square root per covered pixel
d = n_x^2 + n_y^2; covered if d <= 1
n_z = sqrt(1 - d), the near root of the quadratic
normal = (n_x, n_y, n_z), unit length: d + n_z^2 = 1
depth = cz + n_z R (R world units, r pixels)
The silhouette is r pixels across but the depth bulge is R world units, so the impostor is exactly a sphere only where
r = R * zoom * SCALE (Frame::world_sphere). Frame::sphere draws r = max(R * zoom, 3.5), about 18% smaller,
the size the views' spacing was tuned with. Lighting uses the normal in screen axes: the light does not turn with the camera.
the literal pixels of a sphere, r = 20
in (x right, y down, z to viewer);
